parts.name: Processor
parts.role: Runs the autopilot software and the control loop.
parts.whatItDoes: A fast 32-bit processor reads every sensor, works out how the aircraft is moving, and sends a new command to each motor many times a second.
parts.whyItMatters: Processor headroom decides which autopilot software you can run and how many features you can enable at once.
buyingChecks: Check the board has a supported target in your autopilot software
Ask how the supplier sources processors, and from which distributor
Ask whether a processor change would be announced before shipping

parts.name: Inertial sensors (IMUs)
parts.role: Measure rotation and acceleration so the aircraft knows how it is moving.
parts.whatItDoes: Two separate gyroscope and accelerometer chips. Using two lets the autopilot compare them and keep flying if one fails or reads badly.
parts.whyItMatters: Sensor noise and vibration isolation set how stable the aircraft is. They are also where remarked or substituted chips most often appear.
buyingChecks: Check the IMU models against your autopilot's supported list
Ask whether the IMUs are soft-mounted or on the main board
Ask for markings photos from each batch

parts.name: Barometer
parts.role: Measures air pressure to estimate altitude.
parts.whatItDoes: A small pressure sensor that lets the autopilot hold height. It is usually covered with foam to block wind from the propellers.
parts.whyItMatters: A noisy or uncovered barometer makes altitude hold drift, which matters for inspection and mapping work.
buyingChecks: Check the barometer has a foam cover
Check the model is supported by your autopilot
Keep it away from direct propeller wash when mounting
